title: The Ice Cream Truck
clue: A tiny bell rings somewhere in the house, and it is not for you.
reveal: You are the ice cream truck, and your puppy is the whole neighborhood. Ring one soft bell, park the truck somewhere new, and serve a scoop to whoever turns up first.
objective: Run a pretend ice cream truck that parks in a different spot each round and serves two flavors your puppy already eats.
instructions: Choose two 'flavors' from foods your puppy already eats, such as their usual wet food and kibble softened into a paste. Put a small spoonful of each on two small saucers.
Pick a bell with a soft tone: a bike bell or a spoon tapped once on a mug. Keep the sound gentle and short.
Park the truck: carry the saucers to a spot out of sight, such as the next room or a corner of another room. Ring the bell once.
Wait. Do not call. When your puppy arrives, set both saucers down a step apart and let them choose which flavor they try first.
Note the pick on a sticky note menu ('Chicken wins'). Let them finish, then pick up the saucers.
Drive to a new stop: a different corner, a different room, a different surface, all indoors. Ring once and serve again. Three stops is a full route.
Close the truck when your puppy wanders off. Wash the saucers and call the day done.
twist: A single bell ring means the truck has parked somewhere new, and your puppy tracks it down and orders by picking a flavor.
variations: No-bell version: sit down at the new stop and wait for your puppy to find you.
Lick mat truck: serve one flavor on a lick mat at a stop instead of two saucers.
One-room truck: park at three spots inside a single room.
Quiet version: tap the spoon on a bowl softly, or skip the bell and use your puppy's name once.
completion: It counts after one stop where your puppy finds the truck and picks a flavor. Whenever they lose interest, the truck closes.
photoIdea: Your puppy arriving at the truck, nose first toward the saucers. Natural light, no posing.
memoryPrompt: Where did the truck park, and which flavor won?
supplies: A soft bell or spoon and mug
Two foods your puppy already eats
substitutes: No bell? Tap a spoon on a mug once, softly.
dietNotes: Count the scoops out of today's food and use only foods your puppy already eats. Ask your vet about diet and portions.
safety: Serve only foods your puppy already eats, taken from the day's ration, and pick up the saucers when they are finished.
Keep the bell soft and brief. If the sound worries your puppy, skip it and call their name softly.
Serve one puppy at a time if you have other pets, and stay close while saucers are down.
